neighbours.label: the digit opening a second dollar amount in a comparison ('$2.11 and premium $2.86')
fire: Plain was priced at $3.15 and deluxe cost $3.90, so the gap is small.
Basic was sold at $1.20 and large cost $1.75, so few upgraded.
GDP was $204 billion and income per head was $6,120 at the time.
Regular was marked at $4.05 and premium cost $4.60, so most chose regular.
Tea was priced at $2.30 and coffee cost $2.95, so we had tea.
Exports were $88 billion and income per head was $3,410 at the time.
Small was priced at $5.25 and medium cost $5.80, so we took medium.
Unleaded was priced at $3.45 and diesel cost $3.85, so vans cost more.
quiet: Plain was cheap and deluxe cost more, so the gap is small.
Basic was sold out and large cost extra, so few upgraded.
GDP was rising and income per head was growing at the time.
Regular was marked down and premium cost more, so most chose regular.
Tea was cheap and coffee cost more, so we had tea.
Exports were falling and income per head was falling at the time.
Small was cheap and medium cost more, so we took medium.
Unleaded was cheap and diesel cost more, so vans cost more.
